answer: Age in the trust hierarchy is bought with per-identity verified output rather than with elapsed time, so an operator cannot batch his accounts through a queue and must run each one through genuine, individually verified work. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The bridge is the attested output, the crystal the stranger who checks it, and the plume the tier the pair unlocks; the bridge is per identity, the crystal cannot be the farm's own, and the plume is what waiting alone cannot buy. Each head also needs a stranger to attest that work.
